chunks: What al-Shaykh, may Allah تعالى support him, informed us of, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:

In a long hadith, he said: He was asked about a well into which a dog, a mouse, or a pig falls. He said: “All of it is to be drained,” meaning if its color or its taste has changed, as indicated by what has preceded regarding the consideration of forty buckets for these things.

Then he said—I mean Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “If the water overcomes it, then let it be drained for a day until night; then a group of people should stand over it, alternating two by two, and they drain it for a day until night, and it has become pure.”
Then al-Shaykh, may Allah تعالى support him, said: If a man urinates into it, forty buckets are to be drawn from it. This indicates it.

key_terms.أَرْبَعُونَ دَلْوًا: forty buckets, the specified amount to be drawn in a related ruling
key_terms.بِئْرٍ: a well whose water is being discussed in rulings of taharah
key_terms.خِنْزِيرٌ: a pig, mentioned as a source of najasah
key_terms.طَعْمُهُ: its taste, whose change indicates contamination
key_terms.طَهُرَتْ: it became pure after the prescribed draining
key_terms.فَأْرَةٌ: a mouse, mentioned among causes of contamination
key_terms.كَلْبٌ: a dog, mentioned as a source of contamination in the well
key_terms.يُنْزَفُ: it is to be drained out from the well

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a well when a dog, mouse, pig, or urine falls into it in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the purification of well-water when it is contaminated by najasah such as a dog, mouse, pig, or urine. It outlines rulings on draining the well fully or partially depending on the extent of contamination and whether the water’s color or taste has changed. The narration is significant in fiqh discussions of ritual purity and the treatment of contaminated water.
